name: Chasa Retica Spiss
kurzbeschreibung: Chasa Retica in Spiss: Rhaeto-Romanic cultural museum in Austria's highest municipality at 1,653 m above sea level on the border with the Engadin.
beschreibung:
Overview

The fascinating cultural museum Chasa Retica is located in the secluded high-alpine village of Spiss in the Tyrolean district of Landeck at an altitude of 1,653 metres. Spiss is the highest political municipality in the Republic of Austria, clinging to the sunny, steep slopes of the Samnaun valley directly on the national border with Switzerland. Housed in a lovingly restored, centuries-old Engadin farmhouse, the museum is dedicated to the unique Rhaeto-Romanic linguistic and cultural history of this alpine enclave, which was closely intertwined with neighbouring Swiss Graubünden and the Vinschgau for centuries.

Rhaeto-Romanic Heritage & Smuggling Across Borders

The settlement of Spiss took place in the High Middle Ages by Rhaeto-Romanic farmers from the Engadin who cleared and cultivated the rugged high valley. Until the 17th century, Romansh was the predominant language spoken in the village, which is still reflected today in numerous Romanic field and house names. The Chasa Retica (Romansh for 'Rhaetian House') displays typical Engadin stone architecture featuring funnel-shaped splayed windows, sgraffito decorations on the facade, vaulted hallways, and wood-panelled Swiss pine parlours (Arvenstuben). The exhibition documents the austere everyday life of mountain farming families who, prior to the construction of the modern access road in 1980, were often cut off from the outside world for weeks during winter. A major focus is dedicated to historic smuggling across rugged alpine passes to Samnaun: original smugglers' pack frames (Kraxen), contraband such as tobacco, coffee, and silk, along with gripping eyewitness accounts depict the perilous nocturnal treks of villagers through perpetual snow. Traditional folk costumes, sacred artifacts, and antique wooden agricultural tools round off the exhibition.

Visit & Getting There

Chasa Retica in Spiss is open during the summer months from mid-June to mid-October two days a week (Tuesdays and Thursdays from 15:00 to 18:00); guided tours for groups and school classes are offered year-round upon prior telephone reservation. Admission prices (as of the 2025/2026 season): adults approx. €5.00, children and youths (aged 6 to 15) approx. €2.50, toddlers free; discounted with the regional guest card TirolWest Card or the Erlebniskarte Samnaun. Arrival by car: via the Inntalautobahn A12 or S16 to Landeck, continue along the B180 (Reschenstraße) to Pfunds/Kajetansbrücke, turn onto the winding Spisser Landesstraße L348 and travel approximately ten kilometres uphill to Spiss (free parking at the municipal office/village centre). By public transport: ÖBB train to Bahnhof Landeck-Zams, from there take Postbus line 210 to Pfunds and connect to the local valley bus to Spiss.

Tips

The ground floor of the museum has low-barrier access; a traditional wooden staircase leads to the upper sleeping chambers. From the village square in Spiss, savour the breathtaking view across the rugged gorge of the Schergenbach and the three-thousand-metre peaks of the Samnaungruppe. Combine your museum visit with a duty-free shopping trip to the neighbouring Swiss duty-free enclave of Samnaun.
